title_en: Ramadan — Virtues and Acts of Worship
summary: Ramadan is the most blessed month of the Islamic year — the month of fasting, Quran, night prayer, and increased good deeds. Its virtues are established in authentic hadith and its specific acts of worship are well-documented in the Sunnah.
content:
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, the month in which the Quran was revealed, and the month of obligatory fasting. Allah says: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed as guidance for the people' (2:185). It is unmatched among the months in its spiritual significance and the rewards available within it.

## Virtues of Ramadan

**The gates of Jannah are opened and the gates of Jahannam are closed:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When Ramadan enters, the gates of Jannah are opened, the gates of Jahannam are closed, and the devils are chained' (Bukhari 1899, Muslim 1079).

**Every night Allah frees people from the Fire:** 'In every night of Ramadan, Allah has those He frees from the Fire' (Tirmidhi 682 — graded hasan by al-Albani). This release continues through the entire month.

**The reward of good deeds is multiplied:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever does a good deed in Ramadan (nawafil/voluntary acts) is like one who fulfilled an obligation outside of Ramadan, and whoever fulfils an obligation in Ramadan receives the reward of seventy obligations outside of Ramadan' (Ibn Khuzayma 1887 — authenticated by Ibn Khuzayma and Ibn Hibban).

**Sins are forgiven:** 'Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and hoping for reward, his previous sins will be forgiven' (Bukhari 38, Muslim 760). The condition — faith (iman) and seeking reward (ihtisab) — is essential. Fasting as a routine cultural practice without sincere faith and seeking Allah's pleasure does not carry this guarantee.

## The Obligatory Fast

Fasting Ramadan means abstaining from food, drink, marital relations, and anything else that invalidates the fast from the break of dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib). The intention (niyyah) is required before Fajr for the obligatory fast. Allah says: 'So whoever sights the crescent of the month, let him fast it' (2:185).

Those with valid excuses — illness, travel, pregnancy, nursing, extreme old age — are permitted to break the fast and make up missed days (or pay fidya in cases where making up is not possible). 'And whoever is ill or on a journey — then a number of other days' (2:185).

## Acts of Worship in Ramadan

### 1. Qiyam al-Layl — Night Prayer (Tarawih)

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever stands in prayer in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven' (Bukhari 37, Muslim 759). This is the tarawih prayer — performed after Isha in congregation or individually.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed tarawih in congregation for several nights, then stopped out of concern it would become an obligation. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) later organised the community to pray together behind one imam, saying: 'This is a good bid'ah (bid'ah hasanah).' This statement from 'Umar is cited in the bid'ah classification debate; in the Athari view, 'Umar was using 'bid'ah' in its linguistic sense (something new), not its technical sense (prohibited religious innovation), since the act itself had Prophetic precedent.

The number of rak'ahs in tarawih is a matter of scholarly difference: 8 rak'ahs + 3 witr is supported by the practice of 'Aisha (Muslim 738); 20 rak'ahs is reported from the Companions' practice under 'Umar and is the position of the majority of classical scholars across the madhabs. Both are practised in the ummah and neither is condemned.

### 2. Recitation of the Quran

Ramadan is the month of the Quran: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed' (2:185). Jibril used to review the entire Quran with the Prophet once a year, and twice in the last year of the Prophet's life (Bukhari 3554). Increased recitation is one of the most meritorious acts.

The practice of completing the Quran once or more during Ramadan — including in the tarawih prayers — is widely practised and encouraged based on the Prophetic model.

### 3. I'tikaf — Seclusion in the Mosque

I'tikaf — remaining in the mosque for worship during the last ten nights — is a confirmed sunnah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) performed it every Ramadan, and in the year he passed away he performed it for twenty nights (Bukhari 2044). It involves complete devotion to worship: prayer, Quran recitation, dhikr, and du'a.

### 4. Seeking Laylat al-Qadr

Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) is described as 'better than a thousand months' (97:3) — worship on this night carries the reward of worship performed for over 83 years. It falls in one of the odd-numbered nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan, most likely the 27th according to majority scholarly view (though the precise night is not definitively fixed).

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Search for Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan' (Bukhari 2017). The du'a taught for this night: 'Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibb al-'afwa fa'fu 'anni' (Tirmidhi 3513 — sahih).

### 5. Suhur — The Pre-Dawn Meal

'Eat the suhur (pre-dawn meal), for in the suhur there is barakah' (Bukhari 1923, Muslim 1095). Even a few sips of water qualifies. The meal immediately before Fajr is recommended and distinguishes the Muslim fast from other fasting traditions.

### 6. Sadaqah — Charity

'The Prophet was the most generous of people, and he was most generous in Ramadan when Jibril used to meet him' (Bukhari 3554). Increased charity in Ramadan is among the most consistent practices of the Sunnah.

## Laylat al-Qadr

Surah al-Qadr (97) describes this night: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter. Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.'
evidence_quran: Surah al-Baqarah 2:185 — 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed as guidance for the people'
Surah al-Qadr 97:1-5 — full surah on Laylat al-Qadr
Surah al-Baqarah 2:183 — 'O you who have believed, fasting is prescribed for you... that you may attain taqwa'
evidence_hadith: Bukhari 1899, Muslim 1079 — 'When Ramadan enters, the gates of Jannah are opened, the gates of Jahannam are closed, and the devils are chained'
Bukhari 38, Muslim 760 — 'Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven'
Bukhari 37, Muslim 759 — 'Whoever stands in prayer in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven'
Bukhari 2017 — 'Search for Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan'
Bukhari 1923, Muslim 1095 — 'Eat the suhur, for in the suhur there is barakah'
Bukhari 3554 — 'The Prophet was the most generous of people, and most generous in Ramadan'
scholar_positions: The virtues and acts of Ramadan are agreed upon across all schools of Ahl us-Sunnah. The number of tarawih rak'ahs (8 vs 20) is a legitimate scholarly difference; both are practised and neither is condemned. I'tikaf in the last ten nights is a confirmed sunnah. The identification of Laylat al-Qadr with the 27th of Ramadan is the majority scholarly view based on hadith evidence, though the exact night is not conclusively fixed.
